definition: Industrialization is the transformation of an economy from farm and hand labor to machine-driven factory production — a shift that remakes work, towns, and daily life together.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word industrialization. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know industrialization should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Industrialization reached the valley as sound before anything else: the mill whistle at six, where for two centuries there had been only church bells.

Mechanization is the milder change: machines take over a single task in a single workplace — one mill's looms, one cannery's line — while industrialization reorganizes a whole economy's production around the factory.

Automation pushes further than industrialization — industrialization gathers workers around the machines, while automation removes the workers from the loop entirely, the line running with no hands on it.

Urbanization is industrialization's traveling companion — people massing into cities — but the two can part ways: a capital can swell with clerks and courtiers and never build a factory. Industrialization is about how things are produced, not where people crowd.

Modernization swaps old for new on any axis at all — dress, law, plumbing, schooling — and says nothing in particular about machines. Industrialization is one specific engine of it: production moving into machine-driven factories.

When historians describe the island's industrialization, they start with numbers rather than stories.
In 1870 nine of every ten workers farmed or fished; by 1910, most stood at power looms and forge lines in brick mills.
Coal shipments into the main port rose fortyfold in those same decades, and the railways built to move the coal soon moved everything else.
Household spinning wheels, common in every village inventory at mid-century, vanish from the records within a generation.
One ledger says it plainly: what the island made, and how, and by whom, had been rebuilt from the ground up.
